newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU harmonised inflation data for January.
newsitem.headline: EU harmonised inflation data for January.

text.p: Eurostat, the European Commission's statistics office, published for the first time on Friday harmonised inflation figures for all 15 European Union countries.
It issued harmonised price data measured as the annual rates of change (January this year compared with the same month last year).
NOTE - The harmonised inflation data will form the basis for the decision in early 1998 on which countries meet the price stability requirement for economic and monetary union (EMU).
That decision will be based mainly on data for 1997.

According to the EU's Maastricht treaty, a country's average inflation rate observed over a year before the examination should "not exceed by more than 1.5 percentage points that of, at most, the three best performing member states in terms of price stability".
However, analysts are uncertain how this reference value should be calculated.
In a report last November, the European Commission demonstrated six different methods to calculate the rate which should not be exceeded for meeting the price stability criterion.

Out of the six methods and for the purpose of that report it used a method calculating the reference value by taking the unweighted average of the three best performing countries plus 1.5 percentage points.
Regarding the period of one year, two main approaches are possible, according to the EU executive.

One is to use the year-on-year change of monthly inflation indicators and the other is to use the average change of the last twelve months over the preceeding twelve months. In its November report the Commission preferred to use the latter approach, which it did not publish on Friday.
